statement.p: Find the maximum and minimum values of the function f(x)=x-\frac{27x}{x+3} on the interval [0,8].

static.solution: f(x) is the solution to f'(x)=0. The derivative isf'(x)=1-\frac{81}{\left(x+3\right)^{2}}. Setting this equal to zero and solving for x gives x=-3\pm 9, and of these two critical points only -3+9=6 lies in our interval. Evaluating f(-3+9)=f(6) yields the critical value -12. The values of the function at the endpoints of the interval are f(0)=0, f(8)=-11.6364, so the minimum value is -12, and the maximum value is 0.
